title: Introduce staged CI fast-lanes and DepCurator dependency scan
author: Diego Morales
description: Motivation: CI feedback time has regressed as the monolithic workflow runs more heavy integration tests for every PR. This PR introduces a layered/staged CI model: very fast path-aware lanes for lint + unit tests that run on push and PRs (fast-feedback), a medium lane (integration smoke) that runs on PRs but can be cached/queued, and heavy/nightly lanes for long-running end-to-end suites. Additionally, this adds a small tool (DepCurator) that scans workspace dependency graphs to propose candidate removals, flag oversized transitive deps, and annotate PRs with potential savings. The goal is to speed developer feedback, reduce CI resource waste, and give engineering teams automated guidance for dependency pruning. Changes in this PR include: - New .github/workflows/ci-fastpath.yml: path-aware triggers and targeted job matrix. - New .github/workflows/ci-staged.yml: staged lane orchestration with gates and artifact annotations. - tools/dep-curator/: TypeScript scanner action + CLI for local runs. - scripts/ci/affected-packages.ts: faster change detection vs previous workspace scan. - docs/ci/README.md: guidance for adding new modules to fast-lanes and running DepCurator locally. - Dockerfile.ci: small build image tuned for the TS actions to reduce cold-starts. Migration plan: fast-lanes enabled by default for packages in /packages/* and service directories that include a CI fastpath tag in package.json; teams can opt-in/out via .ci-config.yml. DepCurator runs as an optional check and will initially report suggestions (no automated removals). Follow-ups planned: (1) wire DepCurator suggestions to an internal RFC pipeline for safe removals, (2) add license/size gating for release lanes, (3) expose fast-lane metrics in the console. Checklist: - [x] Implement path-aware fast-lane action - [x] Implement staged orchestration and annotated caches - [x] Add DepCurator action and CLI - [x] Update docs and runbook - [x] Run internal dogfood for 48h and iterate Observability: the CI changes produce annotations with estimated tokenized cache sizes and a new metric ci.fastlane.latency in telemetry (sampled) to help tune thresholds. Rollout: merged to main behind feature flag CI_LAYERED_FASTLANES=on.

review_comments: Maya Rangan: Nice separation — can you clarify how flakes in the medium lane bubble back to the PR author?

Diego Morales: DepCurator currently checks package.json/requirements.txt and the lockfile; it marks candidates as 'suggested' and includes context (import counts) to reduce noise. We will add a peer-deps heuristics follow-up.

merge_outcome: Merged to main by Maya Rangan (squash, commit 9f3b2a4). CI_LAYERED_FASTLANES=on feature flag set in infra config.
release_notes: Introduce layered CI (fast/medium/nightly) with path-aware fast-lanes and an initial DepCurator dependency suggestion tool. Improves PR feedback latency and surfaces dependency pruning candidates. No behavioral changes to runtime; opt-in controls available via .ci-config.yml.
additional_context: This PR intentionally keeps DepCurator non-blocking for the first rollout. Teams will receive annotations and can run the CLI locally. The follow-up will wire safe removal automation behind an approval workflow and add stricter gating for release lanes.
